title: Signed tensor-dual evaluation: postcomposition term
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $P,Q$ arbitrary cochain complexes on its bottom-topology one-object ringed site [def-pc-perfect-rhom-base-change-map]. Let $D=\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}(P,A[0])$ [lem-pc-perfect-ring-dual-term-flat], $T=\operatorname{Tot}(D\otimes Q)$ [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], and $H=\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}(P,Q)$ [def-pur-hom-complex]. Fix $n\in\mathbf Z$ and maps $a:T^n\to H^n$, $b:T^{n+1}\to H^{n+1}$ satisfying the signed evaluation conditions [lem-pc-perfect-ring-hom-tensor-degrees] in their respective degrees. Write $\iota_{r,s}$ for the tensor summand inclusion, $d_1,d_2:D^r\otimes Q^s\to T^{n+1}$ for the first and signed second tensor summand differentials, and $\pi_{k,p}$ for the Hom product projection. For every $r,s,p\in\mathbf Z$ with $r+s=n$, $d_2 b\pi_{n+1,p}=\iota_{r,s}a\pi_{n,p}\operatorname{Hom}(1,d_Q^{p+n,p+n+1})$. No boundedness, finiteness, projectivity, or invertibility is assumed.

proof.text: Expand the second total-tensor summand differential with Mathlib HomologicalComplex.mapBifunctor.d₂_eq. If p is not -r, the off-diagonal parts of the two assumed PerfectRingHomTensorDegreeCondition predicates make both sides zero. No existence or invertibility theorem for normalized degree maps is needed.

For p=-r, cancel the inverse tensor-sheafification comparison and use the sheafification adjunction to test on sectionwise pure tensors. Internal-Hom sections are maps on the slice over the unique site object. Use Mathlib CostructuredArrow.mk_surjective to write a slice object as an arrow, IsDiscrete.eq_of_hom to identify its source, and Subsingleton.elim to identify that arrow with the identity. Thus test those maps at the identity object and at x, without restating a slice-uniqueness theorem. Naturality of the tensor comparison and of the sheafification unit carries lambda tensor y to lambda tensor d_Q(y). Evaluate the two assumed normalization predicates on these sections.

Use functoriality of integer-unit scalar multiplication through the two evaluations. The sign identity (-1)^r (-1)^(r*(s+1))=(-1)^(r*s) follows from negOnePow_add and the fact that every integer unit squares to one. Linearity of d_Q moves lambda(x) through the differential. Eliminating equalities of the source and target degree indices proves the eqToHom transport square. This proves the equality on all pure tensors, hence the asserted sheaf-morphism equality.

theorem perfectRingHom_tensorDual_postcomposition {A : Type u} [CommRing A]
    (P Q : CochainComplex (RingSiteModules A) ℤ) (n : ℤ) :
    letI := SheafOfModules.monoidalCategory (CochainComplex.onePointRingSheaf A)
    ∀ (a : (CochainComplex.mapBifunctor (perfectRingDual P) Q (curriedTensor _)).X n ⟶
        (homComplex (R := CochainComplex.onePointRingSheaf A) P Q).X n)
      (b : (CochainComplex.mapBifunctor (perfectRingDual P) Q (curriedTensor _)).X (n + 1) ⟶
        (homComplex (R := CochainComplex.onePointRingSheaf A) P Q).X (n + 1)),
      PerfectRingHomTensorDegreeCondition P Q n a →
      PerfectRingHomTensorDegreeCondition P Q (n + 1) b →
      ∀ (r s p : ℤ) (h : r + s = n),
      HomologicalComplex.mapBifunctor.d₂ (perfectRingDual P) Q (curriedTensor _)
          (ComplexShape.up ℤ) r s (n + 1) ≫ b ≫ ringHomComplexProjection P Q (n + 1) p =
        CochainComplex.ιMapBifunctor (perfectRingDual P) Q (curriedTensor _)
          r s n h ≫ a ≫ ringHomComplexProjection P Q n p ≫
            SheafOfModules.homObjMap (R := CochainComplex.onePointRingSheaf A)
              (𝟙 (P.X p)) (Q.d (p + n) (p + (n + 1)))
